topic: Is it possible to predict the future?

primary_direction.title: Horizon-Conditioned Forecastability and Calibration Atlas
primary_direction.root_mechanism: Forecast information decays with lead time through initial-state uncertainty, model approximation, observation noise, stochastic forcing, and distribution shift; intelligent models can slow or better characterize this decay but cannot create missing information.
primary_direction.intervention_type: design-only rolling-origin multi-domain forecast benchmark with uncertainty perturbations and preregistered horizon tests
falsifiable_conditions: AI fails to improve held-out skill over strong baselines.
Calibration fails under temporal shift while simple recalibration remains stable.
Perturbing observation or initial-condition information does not change estimated effective horizon.
Scenario projections are incorrectly scored as exact event forecasts.
Aggregate scores conceal target-specific horizon collapse.
primary_direction.feasibility: high for public benchmark data and reproducible forecast evaluation; moderate for harmonizing domain timescales and shift annotations

competitive_directions.title: Local divergence horizon
competitive_directions.reason: provides physical error-growth anchor but does not address calibration or socio-technical shift

competitive_directions.title: More compute and larger models
competitive_directions.reason: tests engineering returns but cannot stand for information availability

competitive_directions.title: Conditional scenario futures
competitive_directions.reason: necessary for long-range climate planning but not an exact forecast

competitive_directions.title: General future oracle
competitive_directions.reason: untyped target, leakage-prone, and incompatible with calibrated scientific inference

evolution_checkpoints.change: untyped future -> deterministic, probabilistic, and scenario targets
evolution_checkpoints.reason: prevents category errors and addresses G1

evolution_checkpoints.change: calendar lead time -> normalized lead time relative to domain dynamics
evolution_checkpoints.reason: makes cross-domain horizon comparisons meaningful and addresses G2

evolution_checkpoints.change: single accuracy score -> joint skill, calibration, sharpness, and information gain
model leaderboard -> shift-aware forecastability atlas with baseline and resource controls
evolution_checkpoints.reason: tests whether AI extends useful prediction rather than merely increasing compute
